<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as non Rice Grains

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers non Rice Grains in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: non Rice Grains, as sold (1,138 results), non Rice Grains, flour or meal (238 results), non Rice Grains, cooked (29 results), non Rice Grains, peel or outer layer (5 results) and non Rice Grains, peeled or flesh (5 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-non-rice-grains" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-non-rice-grains-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of non rice grains, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤10</td><td>15–18.6 (bounded)</td><td>24.5–33.1 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>2.96–9.66 (bounded)</td><td>17–19 (bounded)</td><td>24.5–33.1 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>199 reference units; 2 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>193</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>Bielecka et al. 2022</td><td>6</td><td>50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for non rice grains, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Bielecka et al. 2022</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach non Rice Grains

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach non Rice Grains comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Non Rice Grains, as sold from Location B1 (industrial-affected area) had total mercury higher at 56.1 µg/kg, against 0.28 µg/kg for Control (grocery store >55 km from any power plant) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, non Rice Grains, flour or meal from conventional had lead higher at 30,100 µg/kg, against 260 µg/kg for conventional in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that non Rice Grains, as sold from variety EUFM401 (experiment) had Fe higher at 294,000 µg/kg, against 107,000 µg/kg for variety IE3779, raw (control) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2024-nutritional-deficiencies-however-factors-like-antinutrients-influence-|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2024-nutritional-deficiencies-however-factors-like-antinutrients-influence-">nutritional deficiencies. However, factors like antinutrients influence nutrient bioaccessibility. Every source record that names non Rice Grains was decided on its content: 42 occurrence extracted, 42 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Non Rice Grains FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-non-rice-grains" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-non-rice-grains" data-question="What heavy metals are found in non Rice Grains?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in non Rice Grains?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, B, Ba, Ca, CrIII, CrVI, K, Mg, Mo, Na, P, Rb, S and Sr in non Rice Grains, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2024-detection-of-heavy-metals-in-some-edible|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2024</span><a Puścion-Jakubik A, Grabia M, Nowakowski P, Soroczyńska J, Socha K · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Gluten-Free Cereals and Pseudocereals as a Potential Source of Exposure to Toxic Elements among Polish Residents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients 2022, 14, 2342</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/pan2016-zhejiang-vegetables-metals|4]]<span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-non-rice-grains" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-non-rice-grains" data-question="How do heavy metals get into non Rice Grains?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into non Rice Grains?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, non Rice Grains from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than non Rice Grains from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ewa Mozdzer, Renata Gamrat · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals">The Effect of Sludge-Ash Granulates on the Content and Uptake of Heavy Metals by Winter Rape Seeds and Triticale</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Non Rice Grains, as sold from granulate I (experiment) had lead higher at 710 µg/kg, against 370 µg/kg for control (unamended soil, no granulate) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ewa Mozdzer, Renata Gamrat · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals">The Effect of Sludge-Ash Granulates on the Content and Uptake of Heavy Metals by Winter Rape Seeds and Triticale</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mozdzer2023-sludge-ash-granulates-crop-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-non-rice-grains" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-non-rice-grains" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in non Rice Grains?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in non Rice Grains?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, non Rice Grains, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.5 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (110 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in AFRO (1 µg/kg) and the highest in AFRO (210 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-non-rice-grains" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-non-rice-grains" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in non Rice Grains?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in non Rice Grains?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same non Rice Grains.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bielecka J, Markiewicz-Żukowska R, Puścion-Jakubik A, Grabia M, Nowakowski P, Soroczyńska J, Socha K · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Gluten-Free Cereals and Pseudocereals as a Potential Source of Exposure to Toxic Elements among Polish Residents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients 2022, 14, 2342</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Non Rice Grains, flour or meal (product subgroup) had lead higher at 19.3 µg/kg, against 17 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (non rice grains, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bielecka J, Markiewicz-Żukowska R, Puścion-Jakubik A, Grabia M, Nowakowski P, Soroczyńska J, Socha K · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Gluten-Free Cereals and Pseudocereals as a Potential Source of Exposure to Toxic Elements among Polish Residents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients 2022, 14, 2342</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-non-rice-grains-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-non-rice-grains-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in non Rice Grains is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in non Rice Grains is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 31 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Consumer Reports Food Safety and Sustainability Center · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains">Analysis of Arsenic in Rice and Other Grains</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Consumer Reports Food Safety and Sustainability Center</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Consumer Reports Food Safety and Sustainability Center 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 6.2 µg/kg (mean) in non Rice Grains, as sold from all samples.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Consumer Reports Food Safety and Sustainability Center · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains">Analysis of Arsenic in Rice and Other Grains</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Consumer Reports Food Safety and Sustainability Center</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cr-fsasc2014-arsenic-rice-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
